assertion: Initial installation defaults to core only with the management operation; optional initial/later plugin setup shows exact sources/revisions, bindings, effective parameters, adapter status and readiness effects before plugin writes, and confirmation activates exactly the displayed proposal. Known-entry browsing and direct noncatalog source input share the same selection flow; continuing without new plugins preserves a functional core and already installed packages/bindings. The interaction contract defines actual consent, noninteractive/repeat behavior, separate core/plugin transaction outcomes, optional-stage failure recovery and offline/no-write listing or dry-run semantics. Recommendation evidence is an annotation rather than a source allowlist or default selection; an empty eligible set still supports custom source selection and the core-only default. The interaction contract exposes identical generic occurrence/order controls during optional installation and later skill-tree-plugins use: add repeated same-plugin bindings at one anchor, move/configure/remove an exact occurrence, and preview/confirm the complete ordered chain with no plugin-specific restriction.

limits: Design/source review; no external plugin acquisition or invocation.
source_inspection: Existing installer only prompts for flavor; --yes suppresses prompting rather than consenting to plugins.
Existing provider transactions retain separate rows; the design preserves successful rows and blocks optional mutation until all required destinations verify.

The new contract specifies zero-new-plugin defaults, exact proposal/generation/digest confirmation, shared source intake, independently ordered repeated occurrences, frozen parked configuration and separate rollback.
Current unsupported future flags are explicitly marked as design, not executable CLI capability.
